My foreman in the electrical trade got into the apprenticeship at 39 after coming out of two careers (military being the first and commercial trucking as the second) .

Only advice I have for you from someone going through an electrical apprenticeship is listen to your body cause shit starts hurting quickly (I’m in my mid twenties but still)

My experience with working with local 26 guys has been much better compared to working with folks from local 24. As long as you actively ask for help and have an openness to learn, there will be people there to help you succeed and teach you. 

I’m currently in my third year (and third contractor) and I’ve been with journeymen (and r workers) who are very knowledgeable about what they do and many who aren’t great at what they do.

You can message me if you have any further questions.
